title: Audit safeguard ledger for admin actions and retention automation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build an end-to-end 'safeguard ledger' that captures admin-level events (console admin actions, RBAC grants/revokes, config changes, role escalations) and produces tamper-resistant evidence bundles stored in an append-only WORM sink. The ledger must be residency-aware (per-tenant region tags), support legal-hold overrides that extend retention, and expose automated export/playback for compliance auditors. Deliverables include: event ingestion hooks, signed metadata manifests, HSM-backed signing of evidence indexes, a compact immutable index format for fast proof generation, and an export connector to escrow vendors.
acceptance_criteria:
1) All admin action types listed in spec are emitted with consistent schema and residency tags.
2) Evidence bundles are sealed (HSM-signed) and written to WORM store with immutable object keys.
3) Retention policies (tenant-level and legal-hold) are enforced by the retention enforcer without manual intervention.
4) Audit verifier service can produce a cryptographic proof for any exported bundle within <300ms median for 95th percentile requests.
5) Export/playbook button in Console triggers safe snapshot + signed manifest + delivery to escrow; test escrow endpoint receives and validates signature.
6) End-to-end tests and a runbook for incident response are in main repo.
7) Feature flag gated rollout with telemetry: number of bundles sealed, write latency, and export success rate visible in Console.
notes:
Initial spike completed (2025-02-17): validated HSM signing via mock KMS and experimented with content-addressed keys.
Decision (2025-02-21): adopt compact manifest format with canonical JSON + SHA256 tree hashing to keep proofs deterministic across SDKs.
Trade-offs documented: signing every event increases latency; chosen approach batch-sign manifests per 10s window to balance tamper-evidence and request latency for common admin flows.
Operational concern: WORM provider S3 Object Lock vs proprietary escrow; first cut uses S3 Object Lock with retention tags per region and a secondary escrow push for regulatory jurisdictions requiring external custody.
Security note: signing keys live in HSM-backed customer of record KMS; access scoped to a service account; rotation plan included.

implementation_tasks: IN-1: Add admin event hooks to console backend and tag events with residency and request context
IN-2: Implement compact canonical manifest generator and Merkle index builder
IN-3: Integrate HSM-backed signing via KMS SDK and DSSE envelope format
IN-4: Build retention-enforcer service that reconciles tenant policy, legal-hold state, and WORM retention headers
IN-5: WORM writer adapter (S3 Object Lock + provider escrow connector) with retry/backoff
IN-6: Export/playbook endpoint in Console and wire up signed delivery to escrow endpoints
IN-7: E2E tests, chaos tests for early-delete attempts, and performance benchmarks for proof generation
IN-8: Observability: Grafana dashboards + traces + cost breakdown per sealed bundle
risks:
1) Increased request latency for synchronous admin flows; mitigated via batch signing and async write patterns.
2) Cross-region residency constraints may require multiple copies and dual escrow workflows increasing cost.
3) HSM/KMS quotas could throttle signing at scale; will coordinate with infra for quota increases and backpressure strategies.
4) Legal-hold overrides must be authoritative and replicated; includes DB schema migration and migration plan.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Internal beta (5 tenants) behind feature flag; collect telemetry and fix clock skew issues.
Phase 2: Invite-only customer opt-in for Dedicated customers with compliance needs.
Phase 3: Default-on for enterprise tiers after 90-day observation window and Security sign-off.
Backout: feature flag off and immutable bundles remain in WORM; retention-enforcer will keep copies per policy.
qa_test_plan:
1) Simulate console admin action flows and assert bundle creation and signature verification.
2) Simulate legal-hold and attempt deletion; assert retention-enforcer prevents deletion and logs attempted violation.
3) Validate signed manifest at escrow endpoint with HSM public keys.
4) Load test: 2000 admin events/minute and verify sealing throughput and proof generation latency.
5) Clock skew test: introduce +/-10s skew and assert grace window behavior.
definition_of_done: All implementation tasks closed, acceptance criteria met, security review signed, runbook published, and monitoring dashboards operational. PRs merged and release noted in runtime-1.24 changelog.
